content:
Europe funds AI doctoral research better than almost anywhere: salaried contracts in Germany and the Netherlands, high-gross fellowships in Switzerland, tax-free stipends in the UK, and EU-funded networks that let you rotate between countries. This guide maps the fully funded AI PhD routes currently listed on NextApply, what each pays, and which profile fits which route.

The five funding models for an AI PhD in Europe

ModelPay (approx.)Where
Institute fellowshipCHF 73,100–83,500/year (ETH AI Center)Switzerland
Employed doctoral contract€3,010–€4,051/month gross (MP-AIX, Dutch universities)Germany, Netherlands
UKRI-funded CDT stipend£21,805/year, tax-free (+£2,000 London)United Kingdom
EU doctoral network (MSCA DN)≈€3,400/month gross adjusted by countryMulti-country
Erasmus Mundus joint degree€1,400/month + travel & installation2–3 countries

Employee contracts look lower than the ETH fellowship on paper, but they come with pension, health insurance and — in the Netherlands — the possibility of the 30% ruling for foreign employees. UK stipends are lower in cash terms but are tax-free and cover fees separately.

Which route fits your profile

  • Strong ML publication record + top grades: target the ETH AI Center fellowship and MP-AIX first — they are the most competitive and pay the most.
  • Good degree, fewer publications: UK CDTs and Dutch university positions weigh potential and references more heavily; our guide to PhD applications without publications lists dozens of funded routes that do not screen on papers.
  • Interdisciplinary (AI + law, biology, medicine): Erasmus Mundus programmes like EMILDAI and Aithyra are built for cross-domain profiles.
  • Want mobility: MSCA Doctoral Networks rotate you through two or three countries with a standardized allowance — see our MSCA Doctoral Networks guide.

WindowWhat opens

Autumn 2027ETH AI Center and MP-AIX annual calls (expected)

Documents you will need for every route

  1. CV in academic format — our academic CV guide with a full sample.
  2. Transcripts and degree certificates (certified copies; plan 2–4 weeks for issuance).
  3. Two or three reference letters — request them with our email templates.
  4. A research statement tailored to each route (fellowships) or a statement of interest in the group's agenda (CDTs and employed positions).
  5. English evidence: most continental routes accept your prior English-taught degree — see PhD in Germany without IELTS.

Questions applicants often ask

Is a European AI PhD respected in industry? Yes — Max Planck, ETH and Dutch universities are core recruiting grounds for European AI labs, and employee-status PhDs read as work experience.

Can I apply from any country? Every route in the table above is open worldwide; visa support is standard for salaried contracts.

Do I need to already have a research proposal? Only for fellowships. CDTs and employed positions usually ask for a statement of interest instead.

Choosing between offer types (it is not only money)

If the offer is...You getWatch out for
A fellowship (ETH AI Center)Freedom to switch labs, prestige, cohort eventsHigher expectations, one-shot annual calls
An employed position (NL/DE/SE)Pension, unemployment insurance, employee rightsYour project follows the grant that pays you
A CDT place (UK)Structured training, cohort, industry linksStipend ≠ salary: no pension contributions, lower cash
An MSCA DN positionMulti-country rotations, network eventsFixed 3-year horizon; thesis timing pressure
An Erasmus Mundus seatTwo+ degrees, mobility stipend€1,400/month is tight in Northern Europe — budget carefully

Visa basics for AI doctoral hires

  • Germany/Netherlands/Sweden/Denmark/Finland: employed contracts mean standard (fast) work-researcher permits; universities file the paperwork (typically 4–8 weeks).
  • Switzerland: quota-managed but university-administered; ETH/EPFL handle it routinely.
  • UK: student route with recent dependant restrictions; CAS issued after unconditional offer.
  • Austria (Aithyra-type positions): researcher permit with employment contract; processing a few weeks.

Questions applicants often ask (continued)

Should I email supervisors first? For fellowships, no (central admission); for employed positions, yes — a specific email to the grant-holding professor materially raises response rates; templates in our supervisor email guide.

What about internships during the PhD? Employed contracts in NL/DE commonly allow research internships with industry labs — ask before signing, and budget them into your thesis plan (see how to read a PhD job ad for the clauses that matter).
